_comment: THE MANAGER'S CHECKLIST. Every work item in the CURRENT manager session's
scope, and the state of each.
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-01, verbatim in intent: 'every manager session
keeps a detailed checklist of work items in its scope (this may be updated
as work progresses and the workplan is adapted, eg an unforeseen blocker
that needs to be resolved to release the rest of the items) - and every
status update should start with the checklist, then summary of what has
been done (recently) and what's next.'
SO THE REPORTING CONTRACT IS FIXED: checklist -> recently done -> next.
In that order, every time. A status update that opens with a narrative is
not following this.
WHY IT LIVES IN THE REPO AND NOT IN A SESSION'S CONTEXT. Same reason as
MANAGER-LEASE.json and SESSIONS.json: it must survive its holder's DEATH
and be readable by a manager arriving COLD. A checklist held only in
context is lost exactly when a successor most needs it, and re-deriving it
costs the successor the hours that produced it.
IT IS ADAPTIVE, NOT A FROZEN PLAN. The directive is explicit that it
changes as work progresses -- an unforeseen blocker that must be resolved
to release the rest is a first-class edit, not a failure of planning. Add
the blocker as its own item, point the blocked items at it, and say so.
STATES ARE NEVER COLLAPSED. 'delegated' is not 'in progress' and neither is
'done'; 'blocked' names WHAT it waits on. Most importantly 'done' means
MERGED AND OBSERVED, while 'landed_unproven' means the code is in and its
effect has NOT been seen on the fleet -- the distinction this whole system
keeps paying for when it is skipped.
THE MANAGER DOES NOT EXECUTE THESE ITEMS. Operator-directed the same day:
'the manager session only manages and does not take even small items,
because that means they're not focused on what they're actually supposed
to be doing.' An item with owner 'manager' is a MANAGEMENT act (a merge, a
deploy, a lease heartbeat, a spawn), never a build.

states.landed_unproven: merged; effect NOT yet observed on the fleet
states.in_flight: a session is actively working it
states.blocked: waiting on a named thing; see blocked_on
states.queued: scoped and agreed, nobody started it

items.title: The ping duplicate IS real and measured; I archived the session fixing it and told the board it was not
items.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW PREVIOUSLY READ `dropped` WITH 'THE DEFECT WAS NEVER DEMONSTRATED'. THAT WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. The session had already measured it from the live journals: 22:10:19.934 bridge drain tick STARTS, 22:10:21 trader-bot tick reads the SAME file and delivers it, 22:10:23.212 bridge POST returns and unlinks. Both drainers do read -> send -> unlink, so the file survives the whole POST; the bridge's POST took 3.28s against ~1ms on every other tick that day. The copies went to different BOTS because ict-telegram-bot started at 21:37:37Z, before the secret was set at 22:08:26Z, and _resolve_claude_bot() caches once per process. === WHERE MY REASONING FAILED: I read the operator's later 'nothing showed up in both feeds' as REFUTING the earlier 'sent to both channels'. It does not. The mechanism is INTERMITTENT BY CONSTRUCTION — a duplicate needs the winning drainer's POST to exceed the ~2s phase gap between two 5s ticks. Absence on later pings is what the mechanism PREDICTS. === AND THE DUPLICATE IS THE LESS SERIOUS HALF: when the race is won outright one copy is sent, but WHICH CHAT it lands in is decided by scheduler phase, and an operator cannot learn where to look for a channel picked at random. === #10695 reached the same mechanism independently and called it correctly ('predicts intermittent duplication rather than reliable doubling'). Two sessions, same finding, while I had told the board it was not real. === STATUS: #10694 is Tier-2 and stays DRAFT — it changes a live service's drain behaviour and needs ict-telegram-bot.service restarted after merge, which is an operator OK I do not have overnight. FIRST ITEM ON THE MORNING REPORT.

items.title: A superseded pending system-action run is cancelled with NO comment posted back
items.note: Found by the ping test (#10695) when P1b vanished. Three send-ping actions dispatched inside 15s and the MIDDLE run was cancelled: issue left open, zero comments, nothing anywhere saying the action never ran. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects a RUNNING job, but GitHub keeps only one PENDING run per concurrency group, so a third queued run cancels the second. ⚠️ THE ISSUE COMMENT IS THE ONLY RESULT SURFACE A PM-SIDE SESSION HAS, so 'silently dropped' is indistinguishable from 'still queued' — a session can wait forever on a run that is already dead. The test session's workaround was to dispatch strictly one at a time, which is exactly the sort of unwritten discipline that decays. Filed as BL-20260901-SYSTEM-ACTIONS-CANCELS-A-SUPERSEDED-PENDING-RUN-AND-COMMENTS-NOTHING-BACK-SO-A-DISPATCHED-ACTION-IS-SILENTLY-LOST.

items.title: Nine merges in three hours left four PRs conflicted on the same append-mostly register files
items.note:
#10685 was FULLY GREEN at 23:06Z and its merge was REFUSED at 00:15Z with 405 conflicts; #10686, #10687 and #10679 all show ZERO check runs, which here almost always means a conflict rather than 'CI has not started' — the merge ref cannot be built, so the workflows are silently skipped. Cause is simply that main took nine merges tonight and these PRs edit the same append-mostly registers (OPEN-ITEMS.json, the *-backlog.json files, docs/claude/work/*). ⚠️ THE RESOLUTION RULE MATTERS MORE THAN THE RESOLUTION: on an append-mostly register BOTH sides are usually additive and BOTH must survive — dropping the other side's row to clear the conflict deletes the record that something was filed, which is the failure the registers exist to prevent. ⚠️ WORTH A STRUCTURAL FIX RATHER THAN REPEATED CLEANUP: a fast merge queue against hand-edited JSON registers will keep producing this. The manager is absorbing it session-by-session tonight; someone should decide whether these files want an append-only merge driver or a different shape. 

⚠️ UPDATE 2026-09-02T01:11Z — REPRODUCED ON DEMAND, so this is now measured rather than inferred: merging #10685 caused #10707 and #10708 to go `dirty` WITHIN THE SAME MINUTE, both having been fully green minutes earlier. That is the mechanism demonstrated, not merely suspected. Two responses are in flight and they are different in kind: (a) a MITIGATION — the manager's own lease heartbeat moved to a lease-only PR (MI-11), which removes the manager from the blast radius but fixes nothing for anyone else; (b) a DRAIN — the merge train (MI-21) serializing the existing pile. NEITHER IS THE STRUCTURAL FIX. A fast merge queue against hand-edited JSON registers will keep producing this, and the decision between an append-only merge driver, a JSONL shape, or a different store is still unmade and still belongs to the operator.

⚠️ SECOND-ORDER LESSON, recorded because it has now cost this session TWICE in one night: the manager cited this rule with a TRUNCATED backlog id and artifact-validity-guard rejected the PR. Both times the id was copied out of a PR BODY, where a long id renders wrapped — and a PR body is not guard-checked, so the truncation survives there and only fails when it reaches a checked file. The real id is …-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION. THE RULE: never copy a BL/MB/FU id from prose; grep it out of the backlog JSON. This is the 'precedents are not authoritative' rule in its cheapest possible form, and the guard is doing exactly its job — a doc saying 'tracked by BL-X' where BL-X was never filed reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. ⚠️ THE SAME TRUNCATION WAS PASSED INTO THE DRAIN #2 AND #3 SPAWN PROMPTS and cannot be corrected there, because a manager cannot message a running sub-session — so if either cites it, that is the manager's error propagating, not the session's.

items.title: Sub-sessions cannot un-draft or merge, so every PR waits on the one manager
items.note: OBSERVED ACROSS TONIGHT, recorded because it is an OPERATING-MODEL finding rather than a bug, and this cycle's priority is the steering half. MI-20 framed the queue problem as register CONFLICTS. That is real but it is the second-order effect. The first-order fact is that a sub-session can neither UN-DRAFT nor MERGE its own PR — measured tonight, every one of #10686 / #10687 / #10705 / #10679 / #10694 sat as a DRAFT while fully or nearly green, waiting on the single manager. === THE TWO COMPOUND, and that is what makes it worse than either alone: because only the manager merges, merges are SERIALIZED through one actor; and because each merge re-conflicts every other open PR on the append-mostly registers, the serialization is not merely slow, it is QUADRATIC in the number of open PRs. Four merges in ~25 minutes (01:11-01:38Z) each re-dirtied the remainder. === ⚠️ THE DRAFT GATE IS NOT THE BUG AND MUST NOT SIMPLY BE REMOVED. It is what keeps a session from landing its own Tier-2/Tier-3 work unreviewed, and #10679 (order path) and #10694 (needs a service restart) are exactly why it exists. The question worth putting to the operator is narrower: should a session be able to un-draft and merge its OWN Tier-1 PR once CI is green, leaving the draft gate for Tier-2/3? That would take the manager off the critical path for the majority of work without weakening any gate that is actually load-bearing. === Deliberately filed as `triage`, not `queued`: it is a proposal about how the system is operated, so it is the operator's to scope, not the manager's to start.

items.title: The Data Explorer serves the live journal to anyone on the public Caddy host
items.blocked_on: operator — gating a live public read route is Tier-2 and would change what the Svelte SPA can render
items.note: ⚠️ TOP ITEM FOR THE MORNING REPORT, ABOVE THE RETIREMENT DECISIONS. Surfaced by session_01LvzsinECH8HP in #10687 and then MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MANAGER rather than taken on report — plain curl, no Authorization header, from outside the VM against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org : /api/bot/db/table/trades -> HTTP 200, total 5,318 · order_packages -> 200, 4,275 · balance_snapshots -> 200, 29,892. NEGATIVE CONTROL: device_tokens -> HTTP 404, so #10682's exclusion genuinely holds and the probe can distinguish a refusal from a serve. The filing session counted `signals` at 2,301,022 rows. === WHY IT HAPPENED, AND IT IS NOT A CODING ERROR: CLAUDE.md justifies the Data Explorer as Tier-1 on the premise 'no secrets in either DB' — a claim about CREDENTIALS, not about the CONFIDENTIALITY of the trading record. That judgement was made while the API sat on a firewalled IP reachable only server-side by Streamlit. Caddy was then added (2026-08-13) so the browser-direct Svelte SPA could reach the API over HTTPS, and NOBODY RE-DERIVED THE TIER DECISION AFTER THE TRANSPORT CHANGED. The route did not become less safe; the world became able to reach it. === HONEST SEVERITY, in the direction that does not overstate: this is a CONFIDENTIALITY exposure, NOT a control path. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound values and schema-validated identifiers; nothing writes, no order can be placed, and no credential is reachable now that device_tokens is excluded. Nobody's money can be moved with it. What is exposed is the operator's complete trading record — every trade, order package and balance snapshot. === ⚠️ DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED TONIGHT, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Gating a live public read route is Tier-2, and the Data Explorer tab of the Svelte SPA reaches this route BROWSER-DIRECT, so adding a bearer would break a working operator surface. Doing that unannounced at 02:00 while the operator sleeps trades a three-week-old read exposure for a broken dashboard they wake up to. The options worth putting to them: leave it (the record is not secret), gate it behind DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN and teach the SPA to send one, or put Caddy basic-auth in front of /api/bot/db/* only.
